answer: Each agent identity must lock a scarce stake in a public contract before it can earn rewards, and payouts scale with verified work rather than the number of accounts. A random audit can slash the stake when an agent submits duplicated or invalid results, so spawning a nebula of fake identities does not multiply income: each one needs capital and risks losing it. The stake acts as an anchor for accountability; even an umber-sized reward is not worth risking a larger bond.
